answer: A practical sybil defense is to require each agent to lock a deposit tied to a verifiable work history before it can transact. A newcomer starts with a narrow atlas of permissions, such as reading public listings only, and earns wider access as honest trades accumulate. Faking thousands of identities then stops being cheap: each needs its own deposit and slow history, and one fraud can burn the deposit and erase the record. Reputation acts like a velvet rope, easy for proven participants but costly to bypass, because an attacker must cross a canyon of locked capital and wasted time first.
